title.en: Volume 414 Biographies 201: Li Chendian, Xiao Fusi, Zhu Hongzhang, Liu Lianjie, Peng Yuju, Zhang Shiri, Wu Weishou, Zhu Nangui, Luo Fengyuan, Li Xianghe, Xiao Qingyan, Wu Zongguo
title.raw: 卷414 列傳二百一 李臣典 萧孚泗 朱洪章 刘连捷 彭毓橘 张诗日 伍维寿 朱南桂 罗逢元 李祥和 萧庆衍 吴宗国

sentences.zh: =李臣典=李臣典，字祥雲，湖南邵陽人。

translations.literal: Li Chendian. Li Chendian, courtesy name Xiangyun, was a native of Shaoyang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chendian. Li Chendian, whose courtesy name was Xiangyun, came from Shaoyang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 年十八從軍，初隸王珍部下，後從曾國荃援江西，隸吉字營。

translations.literal: At age eighteen he entered the army, first serving under Wang Zhen, later following Zeng Guoquan to relieve Jiangxi, and was assigned to the Ji Character Battalion.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the army at eighteen, first under Wang Zhen, then with Zeng Guoquan’s relief force in Jiangxi, where he served in the Ji Character Battalion.

sentences.zh: 咸豐八年，戰吉安南門外，國荃受重創，臣典大呼挺矛進，追殺至永豐、新淦。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Xianfeng, he fought outside the south gate of Ji’an. Guoquan suffered a severe wound; Chendian shouted and advanced with spear levelled, pursuing and killing the enemy as far as Yongfeng and Xin’gan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1858, during the fighting outside Ji’an’s south gate, Guoquan was badly wounded. Chendian charged forward shouting, spear in hand, and drove the enemy in pursuit all the way to Yongfeng and Xin’gan.

sentences.zh: 國荃奇其勇，超擢寶慶營守備。

translations.literal: Guoquan marvelled at his bravery and promoted him out of turn to garrison commander of the Baoxing Battalion.
translations.idiomatic: Impressed by his courage, Guoquan promoted him ahead of schedule to garrison commander of the Baoxing Battalion.

sentences.zh: 克景德鎮，复浮梁，皆為軍鋒。

translations.literal: In the capture of Jingdezhen and the recovery of Fuliang, he served each time as the army’s vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: He led the van in the capture of Jingdezhen and the recovery of Fuliang.

sentences.zh: 十年，從戰小池驛，晉都司，賜花翎。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he fought at Xiaochi Post Station, was promoted to assistant commander, and was granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: In 1860 he fought at Xiaochi Post Station, rose to assistant commander, and received the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 進規安慶，戰菱湖，逼賊屯，扼其北，國荃傷股墜馬，臣典馳救以歸。

translations.literal: Advancing against Anqing, he fought at Linghu, pressed the rebel encampment, and held its north flank. Guoquan was wounded in the thigh and fell from his horse; Chendian galloped to rescue him and brought him back.
translations.idiomatic: During the advance on Anqing he fought at Linghu, pressed the rebel camp, and sealed off its northern side. When Guoquan was wounded in the thigh and thrown from his horse, Chendian rode to his rescue and carried him off the field.

sentences.zh: 偕張勝祿、張詩日戰樅陽，破援賊，水師得以進屯。

translations.literal: Together with Zhang Shenglu and Zhang Shiri he fought at Zongyang, defeated the relief rebels, and enabled the naval force to advance and encamp.
translations.idiomatic: Alongside Zhang Shenglu and Zhang Shiri he fought at Zongyang, broke the relieving rebel force, and cleared the way for the fleet to move up and take position.

sentences.zh: 十一年，攻安慶西門賊壘，陳玉成糾楊輔清數万人圍官軍數重，戰至日中未決，馳告諸將曰：「事急矣，成敗在此舉！

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, attacking the rebel fort at Anqing’s west gate, Chen Yucheng rallied Yang Fuqing and tens of thousands of men to surround the government army in several rings. The battle reached midday without decision. He galloped to inform the generals, saying: “The situation is urgent; success or failure hangs on this stroke!
translations.idiomatic: In 1861, while assaulting the rebel fort at Anqing’s west gate, Chen Yucheng and Yang Fuqing mustered tens of thousands of men and hemmed the imperial forces in layer after layer. By midday the fight was still undecided. Chendian rode to the other generals and cried, “This is desperate—everything depends on what we do now!

sentences.zh: 」臣典橫槊前驅，與諸營合力決盪，賊大奔，斬首數千級，遂拔安慶，擢參將，賜號剛勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: ” Chendian levelled his spear and led the charge; with the various battalions he joined in a decisive assault. The rebels fled in great disorder, and several thousand heads were taken. Anqing was then captured. He was promoted to brigade general and granted the title Gangyong Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: ” Chendian took the lead with spear couched, and the battalions together delivered a final blow. The rebels broke and ran; thousands were beheaded. Anqing fell, and he was raised to brigade general and given the title Gangyong Batulu.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，從國荃乘勝下沿江各城隘，進軍江寧，臣典會取丹陽鎮，奪秣陵關，以總兵記名。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi, following Guoquan as he pressed his advantage down the Yangtze, taking each fortified town and pass along the river and advancing on Jiangning, Chendian jointly captured Danyang Town and seized Moling Pass, and was entered on the rolls as brigade commander.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 he followed Guoquan’s victorious drive down the Yangtze, reducing fortified posts along the river and marching on Jiangning. Chendian helped take Danyang Town and capture Moling Pass, and was registered as brigade commander.

sentences.zh: 軍中疫作，李秀成大舉來援，逼壘鏖戰，國荃督陣，砲傷頰，臣典與副將倪桂節力衛之，桂節陣亡。

translations.literal: Plague broke out in the army. Li Xiucheng came in force to relieve the city and pressed the fortifications in fierce battle. Guoquan directed the line and was wounded in the cheek by cannon fire. Chendian and deputy commander Ni Guijie fought hard to protect him; Guijie died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: When epidemic sickness swept the camps, Li Xiucheng marched up in strength. The rebels pressed the siege lines in bitter fighting. Guoquan commanded from the front and took a shell wound to the cheek. Chendian and Deputy Commander Ni Guijie fought to shield him; Guijie was killed in action.

sentences.zh: 賊方攻西路急，臣典曰：「此虛聲也，請備東路。

translations.literal: The rebels were pressing hard on the western route. Chendian said: “This is a feint; please prepare the eastern route.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were hammering the western sector. Chendian said, “That is a diversion—hold the east.

sentences.zh: 」既而賊果萃東路，參將劉玉春死之。

translations.literal: ” Before long the rebels indeed massed on the eastern route, and Brigade General Liu Yuchun was killed.
translations.idiomatic: ” Sure enough, the rebels soon concentrated on the east, where Brigade General Liu Yuchun was killed.

sentences.zh: 砲彈穿壁牆如雨注，臣典死守，卒不能入。

translations.literal: Cannonballs pierced the walls like pouring rain. Chendian held firm to the death, and in the end the enemy could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Shells tore through the walls in a steady rain. Chendian held the line at all costs, and the enemy never broke through.

sentences.zh: 圍解，加提督銜。

translations.literal: When the siege was lifted, he was given the brevet rank of provincial military commander.
translations.idiomatic: After the siege was raised, he received the brevet rank of provincial military commander.

sentences.zh: 二年，偕趙三元夜襲雨花台石城，束草填壕，緣梯將上，賊驚覺，燃砲轟擊，軍少卻。

translations.literal: In the second year, together with Zhao Sanyuan he made a night assault on the stone fort at Yuhuatai, bundling straw to fill the moat and climbing ladders to scale the wall. The rebels were roused, lit their guns, and blasted them; the army fell back somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: In 1863 he and Zhao Sanyuan raided the stone fort at Yuhuatai by night, stuffing the ditch with straw bundles and sending men up scaling ladders. The rebels woke, opened fire, and forced a brief withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 臣典搴旗大呼躍而上，諸軍繼之，擲火彈毀敵樓，城立拔，以提督記名。

translations.literal: Chendian seized the standard, shouted, and leapt up; the troops followed. They hurled fire bombs and destroyed the enemy towers; the fort was taken at once, and he was entered on the rolls as provincial military commander.
translations.idiomatic: Chendian snatched the banner, shouted, and scrambled up the wall; the rest of the army poured after him. Fire bombs wrecked the enemy towers, and the fort fell immediately. He was registered as provincial military commander.

sentences.zh: 尋授河南歸德鎮總兵。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was appointed brigade commander of the Guide garrison in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed brigade commander of the Guide garrison in Henan.

sentences.zh: 偕蕭孚泗、張詩日等攻奪紫金山，又敗諸校場，連克近城諸壘。

translations.literal: Together with Xiao Fusi, Zhang Shiri, and others he attacked and took Purple Mountain, then defeated the rebels at the drill grounds and in succession captured the forts near the city.
translations.idiomatic: With Xiao Fusi, Zhang Shiri, and others he stormed Purple Mountain, routed the enemy at the drill grounds, and took one nearby fort after another.

sentences.zh: 三年，克天保城，江寧之圍始合。

translations.literal: In the third year Tianbao Fort was captured, and the encirclement of Jiangning was first closed.
translations.idiomatic: In 1864 Tianbao Fort fell, and the ring around Jiangning was finally closed.

sentences.zh: 五月，克地保城。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Dibao Fort was captured.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Dibao Fort was taken.

sentences.zh: 六月，諸軍番休進攻，賊死拒，殺傷相當。

translations.literal: In the sixth month the armies attacked in rotation by shifts. The rebels resisted to the death, and casualties on both sides were about equal.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the armies assaulted in rotating shifts. The rebels fought to the last man, and losses mounted on both sides.

sentences.zh: 臣典偵知賊糧未盡，諸軍苦戰力漸疲，謂國荃曰：「師老矣！

translations.literal: Chendian learned by reconnaissance that the rebels’ grain was not yet exhausted, while the armies, worn by hard fighting, were growing weary. He said to Guoquan: “The troops are worn!
translations.idiomatic: Chendian’s scouts reported that the rebels still had grain in store while his own men, ground down by ceaseless fighting, were tiring. He told Guoquan, “The army is exhausted!

sentences.zh: 不急克，日久且生變。

translations.literal: If we do not press to capture it quickly, in time troubles will arise.
translations.idiomatic: If we do not take the city soon, trouble will breed with delay.

sentences.zh: 請於龍膊子重掘地道，原獨任之。

translations.literal: I ask to reopen the tunnel at Longbozi and take sole charge of it.
translations.idiomatic: Let me reopen the tunnel at Longbozi—I will bear the task alone.

sentences.zh: 」遂率副將吳宗國等日夜穴城，十五日地道成，臣典與九將同列誓狀。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon he led Deputy Commander Wu Zongguo and others day and night in tunneling under the wall. On the fifteenth day the tunnel was complete; Chendian and nine generals jointly submitted written oaths.
translations.idiomatic: ” He then led Deputy Commander Wu Zongguo and others, tunneling day and night. On the fifteenth day the mine was ready; Chendian and nine generals signed a joint oath on penalty of death.

sentences.zh: 翼日，地雷發，臣典等蟻附入城，諸軍畢入。

translations.literal: The next day the land mine was fired; Chendian and the others swarmed into the city like ants, and all the armies entered.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the mine blew; Chendian and his men poured through the breach like ants, and the whole army followed in.

sentences.zh: 下令見長發者、新薙發者皆殺，於是殺賊十餘萬人。

translations.literal: He ordered that anyone seen with long hair or newly shorn hair was to be killed; thus more than a hundred thousand rebels were slain.
translations.idiomatic: He gave orders to kill anyone with long hair or a fresh shave; in this way more than a hundred thousand rebels were put to the sword.

sentences.zh: 臣典遽病，恃壯不休息，未幾，卒於軍，年二十七。

translations.literal: Chendian suddenly fell ill; relying on his strength, he would not rest, and before long he died in camp at the age of twenty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Chendian fell suddenly ill. Trusting in his youth, he refused to rest, and soon died in camp at twenty-seven.

sentences.zh: 捷上，列臣典功第一，錫封一等子爵，賜黃馬褂、雙眼花翎。

translations.literal: When the victory report was submitted, Chendian’s merit was ranked first; he was enfeoffed as first-rank viscount, and granted the yellow jacket and double-eyed peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: In the victory memorial Chendian’s service was placed first. He was ennobled as a first-rank viscount and awarded the yellow jacket and double-eyed peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 命未至而臣典已歿，詔加贈太子少保，諡忠壯，吉安、安慶、江寧各建專祠。

translations.literal: The order had not yet arrived when Chendian had already died. An edict posthumously promoted him to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, gave him the posthumous name Zhongzhuang, and ordered separate shrines built at Ji’an, Anqing, and Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: The decree had not reached him before he died. The court posthumously made him Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, gave him the posthumous name Loyal and Valiant, and erected dedicated shrines at Ji’an, Anqing, and Jiangning.

sentences.zh: =蕭孚泗=蕭孚泗，湖南湘鄉人。

translations.literal: Xiao Fusi. Xiao Fusi was a native of Xiangxiang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Fusi. Xiao Fusi came from Xiangxiang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，入湘軍，從羅澤南轉戰江西、湖北，洊擢守備。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng he entered the Hunan Army, followed Luo Zinan in campaigns through Jiangxi and Hubei, and was repeatedly promoted to garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: In 1853 he joined the Hunan Army and campaigned with Luo Zinan through Jiangxi and Hubei, rising by repeated promotion to garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 六年，從曾國荃援江西，克安福、吉水、萬安諸縣。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he followed Zeng Guoquan to relieve Jiangxi and captured the counties of Anfu, Jishui, and Wan’an.
translations.idiomatic: In 1856 he marched with Zeng Guoquan to relieve Jiangxi and took the counties of Anfu, Jishui, and Wan’an.

sentences.zh: 七年，克峽江，擢游擊，賜花翎。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he captured Xiajiang, was promoted to mobile corps commander, and was granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: In 1857 he took Xiajiang, was made mobile corps commander, and received the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 八年，從攻吉安，賊出撲孚泗營，開壁奮擊，斃悍賊多名。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, in the attack on Ji’an, the rebels came out and rushed Fusi’s camp. He opened the stockade and fought fiercely, killing many fierce rebels.
translations.idiomatic: In 1858, during the siege of Ji’an, rebels sallied against Fusi’s camp. He threw open the gates and counterattacked, killing many of their best fighters.

sentences.zh: 旋克吉安，擢參將。

translations.literal: Ji’an was soon captured, and he was promoted to brigade general.
translations.idiomatic: Ji’an fell soon after, and he was promoted to brigade general.

sentences.zh: 九年，江西肅清，擢副將。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Jiangxi was pacified, and he was promoted to deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: In 1859, when Jiangxi was cleared, he was raised to deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 會攻太湖，十年春，大戰小池驛，复太湖，孚泗功多，賜號勷勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: He joined the attack on Taihu. In the spring of the tenth year there was a great battle at Xiaochi Post Station; Taihu was recovered, and Fusi’s merit was great. He was granted the title Xiangyong Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the assault on Taihu. In the spring of 1860 he fought a major action at Xiaochi Post Station and helped recover the lake district. For his outstanding service he received the title Xiangyong Batulu.

sentences.zh: 進攻安慶，戰菱湖，孚泗於東路橫壕倚水築新營，會擊屢破賊。

translations.literal: Advancing against Anqing, he fought at Linghu. On the eastern route Fusi dug trenches across the line, built a new camp leaning on the water, and in joint attacks repeatedly defeated the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: In the advance on Anqing he fought at Linghu. On the eastern front Fusi cut trenches along the waterline, threw up a new camp, and in repeated combined strikes broke the rebel forces.

sentences.zh: 分道攻安慶城外諸壘，賊援迭至，與城賊相應，更番撲官軍營壘，孚泗等且戰且築壘，賊不得逞；

translations.literal: Forces were divided to attack the various forts outside Anqing’s walls. Rebel relief came in succession and coordinated with the garrison; they took turns rushing the government camps. Fusi and others fought while building forts, and the rebels could not prevail;
translations.idiomatic: Columns were sent against the outworks around Anqing. Rebel reinforcements arrived in waves and coordinated with the garrison, assaulting imperial camps in rotation. Fusi and his men fought while throwing up new works, and the rebels gained no advantage;

sentences.zh: 又偕水師副將蔡國祥截獲賊糧。

translations.literal: he also joined Naval Deputy Commander Cai Guoxiang in intercepting rebel grain supplies.
translations.idiomatic: he also worked with Naval Deputy Commander Cai Guoxiang to seize rebel grain convoys.

sentences.zh: 八月，以地雷壞城，復安慶，以總兵記名。

translations.literal: In the eighth month a land mine breached the wall; Anqing was recovered, and he was entered on the rolls as brigade commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month a mine brought down the wall and Anqing was retaken; he was registered as brigade commander.

sentences.zh: 加提督銜，授河南歸德鎮總兵。

translations.literal: He was given the brevet rank of provincial military commander and appointed brigade commander of the Guide garrison in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He received the brevet rank of provincial military commander and was appointed brigade commander of the Guide garrison in Henan.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，國荃循江東下，孚泗為前鋒，攻拔西梁山。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi, as Guoquan followed the river eastward, Fusi served as vanguard and attacked and took West Liang Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862, as Guoquan drove down the Yangtze, Fusi led the van and stormed West Liang Mountain.

sentences.zh: 會水師克太平、蕪湖，破金柱關、東梁山，進克秣陵關、江心洲，乘勝逼江寧，以提督記名。

translations.literal: Together with the fleet he captured Taiping and Wuhu, broke Jinzhu Pass and East Liang Mountain, advanced to take Moling Pass and Jiangxin Island, pressed the advantage against Jiangning, and was entered on the rolls as provincial military commander.
translations.idiomatic: Coordinating with the fleet, he took Taiping and Wuhu, broke Jinzhu Pass and East Liang Mountain, then seized Moling Pass and Jiangxin Island and pressed on toward Jiangning. He was registered as provincial military commander.

sentences.zh: 李秀成來援，分黨趨江心洲截運道，孚泗等逆擊敗之。

translations.literal: Li Xiucheng came to relieve the city; detachments moved toward Jiangxin Island to cut the supply route. Fusi and others met them in counterattack and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiucheng marched to the rescue and sent columns toward Jiangxin Island to sever the supply line. Fusi and his men counterattacked and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 賊攻孚泗後營砲台，相持十餘日，賊以地雷毀營牆，孚泗以火藥數十桶擲轟，賊不得入。

translations.literal: The rebels attacked the gun platform at Fusi’s rear camp; the standoff lasted more than ten days. The rebels used a land mine to destroy the camp wall. Fusi hurled dozens of barrels of gunpowder in explosion, and the rebels could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels assaulted the gun platform at Fusi’s rear camp for more than ten days. When a mine blew in the wall, he rolled dozens of powder kegs into the breach and blasted the attackers back.

sentences.zh: 伺賊疲，孚泗與彭毓橘突出夾擊，踏平賊壘數十，賜黃馬褂。

translations.literal: Watching for the rebels to tire, Fusi and Peng Yuju sallied forth in a pincer attack and levelled several tens of rebel forts; he was granted the yellow jacket.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels flagged, Fusi and Peng Yuju charged out in a pincer and flattened dozens of enemy works. He was awarded the yellow jacket.

sentences.zh: 二年，偕總兵李臣典襲克雨花台石城，追至上方橋，斬馘數千，又破秣陵關賊卡。

translations.literal: In the second year, together with Brigade Commander Li Chendian he stormed and took the stone fort at Yuhuatai, pursued to Shangfang Bridge, and beheaded several thousand; he also broke the rebel stockade at Moling Pass.
translations.idiomatic: In 1863 he and Brigade Commander Li Chendian stormed the stone fort at Yuhuatai, pursued the enemy to Shangfang Bridge, and killed thousands; he also overran the rebel post at Moling Pass.

sentences.zh: 夜襲上方橋，結筏渡河，扼雙橋門，連破賊隘。

translations.literal: He made a night assault on Shangfang Bridge, lashed rafts to cross the river, held Shuangqiao Gate, and in succession broke rebel passes.
translations.idiomatic: In a night attack on Shangfang Bridge he rafted the river, seized Shuangqiao Gate, and took one rebel pass after another.

sentences.zh: 偕彭毓橘縱火焚其橋，襲賊屯，擢福建陸軍提督。

translations.literal: Together with Peng Yuju he set fire and burned their bridge, raided the rebel encampment, and was promoted to provincial commander of the Fujian Army.
translations.idiomatic: With Peng Yuju he burned the bridge by fire, stormed the rebel camp, and was made provincial commander of the Fujian Army.

sentences.zh: 三年，既克天保城，孚泗出鍾山北，於太平門築三壘守之，絕賊糧道。

translations.literal: In the third year, after Tianbao Fort was taken, Fusi went out north of Bell Mountain, built three forts at Taiping Gate to hold them, and cut off the rebels’ grain route.
translations.idiomatic: In 1864, once Tianbao Fort had fallen, Fusi moved north of Bell Mountain, threw up three forts at Taiping Gate, and severed the rebels’ supply line.

sentences.zh: 六月，進占龍膊子山石城，孚泗與李臣典築砲台山上，距城僅十餘丈，積沙草高與城齊，作偽攻狀，潛於其下鑿地道。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he advanced and occupied the stone fort on Longbozi Mountain. Fusi and Li Chendian built gun platforms on the hill, only a dozen-odd zhang from the wall, heaped sand and straw as high as the wall to feign assault, and secretly tunneled beneath.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he seized the stone fort on Longbozi Mountain. Fusi and Li Chendian built batteries on the heights barely thirty yards from the wall, piled sand and straw level with the ramparts to simulate an assault, and dug a tunnel underneath.

sentences.zh: 賊宵攻毀砲台，副將陳萬勝戰死，明日，會師逼城下，總兵郭鵬程、王紹羲復中砲死。

translations.literal: The rebels attacked by night and destroyed the gun platforms; Deputy Commander Chen Wansheng died in battle. The next day the united armies pressed under the wall; Brigade Commanders Guo Pengcheng and Wang Shaoyi were again killed by cannon fire.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels struck by night and wrecked the batteries; Deputy Commander Chen Wansheng was killed. The next day the combined force pressed to the foot of the wall, and Brigade Commanders Guo Pengcheng and Wang Shaoyi were killed by shellfire.

sentences.zh: 及地道成，火發城圮，將士爭登，賊擲火藥抵拒，死僕相繼。

translations.literal: When the tunnel was complete, fire was set and the wall collapsed; officers and men scrambled to climb up. The rebels hurled gunpowder to resist, and the dead fell one after another.
translations.idiomatic: When the mine was ready, the blast brought down the wall and men scrambled up the breach. Rebels hurled powder bombs in reply, and bodies piled up in the assault.

sentences.zh: 孚泗手刃退者數人，士氣乃奮，盡從缺口入。

translations.literal: Fusi personally killed several who fell back; morale then surged, and all entered through the breach.
translations.idiomatic: Fusi himself cut down several men who wavered; spirits rallied, and the troops poured through the breach.

sentences.zh: 李秀成匿民舍，孚泗索獲之，並擒洪仁達。

translations.literal: Li Xiucheng hid in a civilian house; Fusi searched him out and captured him, and also seized Hong Renda.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiucheng hid in a private house; Fusi tracked him down and took him, along with Hong Renda.

sentences.zh: 論功，賜封一等男爵，賜雙眼花翎。

translations.literal: In reckoning merit he was enfeoffed as first-rank baron and granted the double-eyed peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was ennobled as a first-rank baron and given the double-eyed peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 尋丁父憂歸。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he returned home in mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: He soon went home to observe mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 光緒十年，卒於家，優恤，諡壯肅。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Guangxu he died at home; generous condolence gifts were granted, and he was given the posthumous name Zhuangsu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1884 he died at home. The court granted generous funeral honors and the posthumous name Valiant and Stern.

sentences.zh: =朱洪章=朱洪章，字煥文，貴州黎平人。

translations.literal: Zhu Hongzhang. Zhu Hongzhang, courtesy name Huanwen, was a native of Liping in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Hongzhang. Zhu Hongzhang, whose courtesy name was Huanwen, came from Liping in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 咸豐初，應募為鄉勇，從黎平知府胡林翼剿新寧竄匪，又剿黃平榔匪，擒匪首劉瞎麼，以功獎外委。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianfeng he enlisted as a village militiaman, followed Liping Prefect Hu Linyi in suppressing bandits who had fled into Xinning, and also suppressed the Lang bandits of Huangping, capturing the bandit chief Liu Xiame; for his merit he was rewarded with the rank of external deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xianfeng reign he joined the local militia and served under Liping Prefect Hu Linyi against bandits raiding from Xinning and against the Lang bandits of Huangping, capturing their leader Liu Xiame. He was rewarded with the rank of external deputy.

sentences.zh: 四年，從林翼援湖北，會克岳州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he followed Linyi to relieve Hubei and jointly captured Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1854 he marched with Linyi to relieve Hubei and helped take Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 從塔齊布攻武昌，破賊洪山，遂隸塔齊布軍。

translations.literal: He followed Taqibu in the attack on Wuchang, defeated the rebels at Hongshan, and then was attached to Taqibu’s army.
translations.idiomatic: He fought under Taqibu at Wuchang, routed the rebels at Hongshan, and thereafter served in Taqibu’s command.

sentences.zh: 戰大冶、半壁山、田家鎮、孔壟、小池口，攻九江，無役不從，以勇名。

translations.literal: He fought at Daye, Banbishan, Tianjiazhen, Konglong, and Xiaochikou, and attacked Jiujiang; there was no campaign from which he was absent, and he was famed for courage.
translations.idiomatic: He fought at Daye, Banbishan, Tianjiazhen, Konglong, and Xiaochikou and joined the assault on Jiujiang, missing no battle and earning a name for bravery.

sentences.zh: 塔齊布卒，從周鳳山。

translations.literal: When Taqibu died, he followed Zhou Fengshan.
translations.idiomatic: After Taqibu’s death he served under Zhou Fengshan.

sentences.zh: 鳳山敗，隸畢金科。

translations.literal: When Fengshan was defeated, he was attached to Bi Jinke.
translations.idiomatic: When Fengshan’s force was broken, he joined Bi Jinke.

sentences.zh: 六年，克饒州，擢千總。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he captured Raozhou and was promoted to company commander.
translations.idiomatic: In 1856 he took Raozhou and was promoted to company commander.

sentences.zh: 金科戰歿，代領其軍。

translations.literal: Jinke died in battle, and he took command of his army in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: When Jinke fell in battle, Hongzhang took over his command.

sentences.zh: 江西不給餉，張芾倚蔽皖南，資之，軍始不散。

translations.literal: Jiangxi did not provide pay; Zhang Fu, relying on the screen of southern Anhui, supplied him, and only then did the army not disperse.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi paid no rations, but Zhang Fu, shielded by southern Anhui, supported him, and the force held together.

sentences.zh: 又以會攻四十里街，他將敗績，被劾，降把總。

translations.literal: Also, because in a joint attack on Sishili Street other generals suffered defeat, he was impeached and reduced to platoon commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was also impeached and demoted to platoon commander after a joint assault on Sishili Street ended in defeat for the other commanders.

sentences.zh: 九年，從曾國荃复景德鎮，复官，以守備補用。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he followed Zeng Guoquan in recovering Jingdezhen, was restored to office, and was appointed acting garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: In 1859 he followed Zeng Guoquan in retaking Jingdezhen, was restored to rank, and appointed acting garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 遂從曾國荃部下，戰績始著。

translations.literal: Thereafter he served under Zeng Guoquan, and his battle achievements first became notable.
translations.idiomatic: He then served under Zeng Guoquan, and his record in battle began to stand out.

sentences.zh: 十年，從攻太湖，解小池驛之圍，晉都司。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he joined the attack on Taihu, relieved the siege at Xiaochi Post Station, and was promoted to assistant commander.
translations.idiomatic: In 1860 he joined the Taihu campaign, lifted the siege at Xiaochi Post Station, and was made assistant commander.

sentences.zh: 進攻安慶，爭壕奪壘，斬刈甚多。

translations.literal: Advancing against Anqing, he contested trenches and seized forts, killing and mowing down many.
translations.idiomatic: In the advance on Anqing he fought for trenches and forts and killed a great many of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 十一年，克安慶，超擢參將，賜號勤勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Anqing was captured; he was promoted out of turn to brigade general and granted the title Qinyong Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1861 Anqing fell; he was promoted ahead of schedule to brigade general and given the title Qinyong Batulu.

sentences.zh: 從國荃由皖東下，連奪沿江要隘，擢副將。

translations.literal: Following Guoquan eastward from Anhui, he in succession seized key passes along the river and was promoted to deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: Marching east from Anhui with Guoquan, he took one strategic pass after another along the Yangtze and was raised to deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 進屯雨花台，江寧城賊出撲，屢擊破之。

translations.literal: Advancing he encamped at Yuhuatai; rebels from Jiangning city came out and rushed him, and he repeatedly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced and encamped at Yuhuatai. Garrison troops from Jiangning sallied against him again and again, and he beat them back each time.

sentences.zh: 及援賊至，大營被圍，迭以地雷毀營牆，悍賊擁入，口銜利刃，匍匐而進。

translations.literal: When relief rebels arrived, the main camp was surrounded; land mines were used repeatedly to destroy the camp walls. Fierce rebels crowded in, blades held in their mouths, crawling forward on their bellies.
translations.idiomatic: When relieving forces arrived, the main camp was encircled. Mines blew gap after gap in the walls, and elite rebels poured through, blades gripped in their teeth, crawling forward on their bellies.

sentences.zh: 洪章督隊發槍砲，擲火焚燒，斃賊無算，傷亡士卒甚多，久之始解。

translations.literal: Hongzhang directed his companies in firing muskets and cannon, hurling fire to burn them, and killed rebels beyond counting; many officers and men were wounded or killed, and only after a long time was the siege lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhang led his men in musket and cannon fire and hurled fire bombs, killing untold numbers of rebels at the cost of heavy casualties. Only after a long ordeal was the encirclement broken.

sentences.zh: 洪章先以迭克城隘，以總兵記名，至是加提督銜。

translations.literal: Hongzhang had earlier, for repeatedly capturing city passes, been entered on the rolls as brigade commander; at this time he was given the brevet rank of provincial military commander.
translations.idiomatic: He had already been registered as brigade commander for taking pass after pass around the city; now he received the brevet rank of provincial military commander.

sentences.zh: 同治三年，攻江寧久不拔，及開地道於龍膊子山麓告成，議推前鋒。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tongzhi, the attack on Jiangning had long failed to succeed; when the tunnel opened at the foot of Longbozi Mountain was completed, they deliberated on who should lead the assault.
translations.idiomatic: In 1864 the siege of Jiangning had dragged on without success. When the tunnel at the foot of Longbozi Mountain was finished, the generals debated who should lead the assault.

sentences.zh: 國荃召諸將署名具軍令狀，洪章署第一，武明良第二，劉連捷第三，其他以次署畢，共得九人。

translations.literal: Guoquan summoned the generals to sign and submit military oaths. Hongzhang signed first, Wu Mingliang second, Liu Lianjie third; the others signed in order, nine in all.
translations.idiomatic: Guoquan called the generals to sign written oaths on penalty of death. Hongzhang signed first, Wu Mingliang second, Liu Lianjie third, and six others followed, nine in all.

sentences.zh: 發火城崩，洪章率所部長、勝、煥字三營千五百人，從倒口首先沖入，賊倉猝從城頭擲火藥傾盆下，士卒死四百餘人。

translations.literal: When the fire was set the wall collapsed. Hongzhang led fifteen hundred men of his Chang, Sheng, and Huan Character battalions and charged first through the breach; the rebels in panic hurled gunpowder from the wall in torrents, and more than four hundred soldiers died.
translations.idiomatic: The mine blew and the wall came down. Hongzhang led fifteen hundred men of his Chang, Sheng, and Huan battalions through the breach at the head of the assault. Rebels on the wall rained powder down in sheets, and more than four hundred of his men were killed.

sentences.zh: 洪章入城後，結圜陣與賊排擊。

translations.literal: After Hongzhang entered the city, he formed a circular formation and engaged the rebels in ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Once inside the city, Hongzhang formed a ring formation and fought the rebels rank by rank.

sentences.zh: 諸將畢入，乃分軍為三，洪章趨中路，直攻天王府之北，短兵巷戰一日夜，搜斬逆酋尤眾，賜黃馬褂，予騎都尉世職，無論提鎮缺出，侭先題奏。

translations.literal: When all the generals had entered, the army was divided into three. Hongzhang pressed the center route, attacking straight north of the Heavenly King’s Palace. Close combat in the lanes lasted a day and a night; he searched out and beheaded rebel chiefs in especially great numbers. He was granted the yellow jacket, given the hereditary office of Cavalry Commandant, and regardless of which provincial commander or brigade post fell vacant, he was to be memorialized first.
translations.idiomatic: After every commander was inside, the force split three ways. Hongzhang took the center and drove straight on the north side of the Heavenly King’s Palace. Hand-to-hand fighting in the alleys lasted a full day and night; he hunted down and killed an especially large number of rebel leaders. He received the yellow jacket, a hereditary Cavalry Commandant post, and priority nomination whenever a provincial or brigade command opened.

sentences.zh: 初敘入城功，李臣典以決策居第一，洪章列第三，眾為不平。

translations.literal: When merit for entering the city was first reckoned, Li Chendian was ranked first for his decision-making, and Hongzhang third; many felt this was unjust.
translations.idiomatic: In the first tally of merit for the assault, Li Chendian was placed first for planning the mine, Hongzhang third, and many thought that unfair.

sentences.zh: 洪章曰：「吾一介武夫，由行伍擢至總鎮。

translations.literal: Hongzhang said: “I am but a common soldier of arms, raised from the ranks to brigade commander.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhang said, “I am only a fighting man promoted from the ranks to brigade commander.

sentences.zh: 今幸東南底定，百戰餘生，荷天寵錫，已叨非分，又何求焉？

translations.literal: Now fortunately the southeast is settled; I have survived a hundred battles and received Heaven’s favor—already more than my due. What more could I seek?
translations.idiomatic: Now that the southeast is pacified, I have survived a hundred battles and received more favor from Heaven than I deserve. What more could I ask?

sentences.zh: 四年，授湖南永州鎮總兵。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed brigade commander of the Yongzhou garrison in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1865 he was appointed brigade commander of the Yongzhou garrison in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 光緒二年，調雲南鶴麗鎮，署昭通、臨安、騰越諸鎮。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangxu he was transferred to the Heli garrison in Yunnan and acted as commander of the Zhaotong, Lin’an, and Tengyue garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: In 1876 he was transferred to the Heli garrison in Yunnan and served in acting command at Zhaotong, Lin’an, and Tengyue.

sentences.zh: 鶴麗地卑下，水潦常沒民田，有新河洩水，通塞無常。

translations.literal: The Heli region is low-lying; floods often submerged the people’s fields. There was a New River to drain the water, but whether it was open or blocked was irregular.
translations.idiomatic: Heli lay in low country where floods often drowned the fields. A New River was meant to carry off the water, but it silted up and cleared unpredictably.

sentences.zh: 洪章在鎮，躬率士卒開濬數次，水患為紓，民感之。

translations.literal: While Hongzhang was in command, he personally led the soldiers in dredging several times; the flood peril was eased, and the people were grateful.
translations.idiomatic: At his post Hongzhang personally led troops in dredging the channel several times, easing the floods, and the people were grateful.

sentences.zh: 十四年，因病乞開缺，病痊，曾國荃調留兩江，洪章憑弔龍膊子山，祭死士瘞所，國荃為樹碑紀事。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, ill, he requested leave from office. When he recovered, Zeng Guoquan summoned him to remain in the Two Jiangs. Hongzhang went to mourn at Longbozi Mountain and offered sacrifice at the burial place of the dead soldiers; Guoquan erected a stele to record the event.
translations.idiomatic: In 1888 he fell ill and asked to resign his post. After he recovered, Zeng Guoquan kept him in the Two Jiangs region. Hongzhang visited Longbozi Mountain to mourn and sacrificed at the burial ground of the fallen; Guoquan set up a stele to commemorate the occasion.

sentences.zh: 十五年，署狼山鎮總兵。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he acted as brigade commander of the Langshan garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In 1889 he served as acting brigade commander of the Langshan garrison.

sentences.zh: 二十年，張之洞檄募十營防金沙衛。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year Zhang Zhidong issued orders to recruit ten battalions to garrison Jinshawei.
translations.idiomatic: In 1894 Zhang Zhidong ordered him to raise ten battalions to defend Jinshawei.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，卒於軍。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he died in camp.
translations.idiomatic: In 1895 he died on active service.

sentences.zh: 之洞疏陳戰績，稱其收復江寧，功實第一。

translations.literal: Zhidong memorialized his battle achievements, stating that in recovering Jiangning his merit was truly first.
translations.idiomatic: Zhidong reported his campaigns to the throne, declaring that in the recovery of Jiangning his service ranked first.

sentences.zh: 詔宣付史館，從優議卹，諡武慎，附祀曾國籓、國荃、胡林翼專祠。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the account transmitted to the Historiographical Institute, generous condolence gifts to be deliberated, the posthumous name Wushen granted, and attendant sacrifice at the dedicated shrines of Zeng Guofan, Guoquan, and Hu Linyi.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered his record sent to the Historiographical Institute, generous funeral honors granted, the posthumous name Martial and Cautious bestowed, and his spirit enshrined alongside those of Zeng Guofan, Zeng Guoquan, and Hu Linyi.

sentences.zh: =劉連捷=劉連捷，字南雲，湖南湘鄉人。

translations.literal: Liu Lianjie. Liu Lianjie, courtesy name Nanyun, was a native of Xiangxiang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Lianjie. Liu Lianjie, whose courtesy name was Nanyun, came from Xiangxiang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 以外委隸同族劉騰鴻湘後營，轉戰湖北。

translations.literal: As an external deputy he was attached to the Rear Battalion of the Hunan Army under his clansman Liu Tenghong, and fought in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: Serving as an external deputy, he joined the Hunan Army's Rear Battalion under his kinsman Liu Tenghong and saw action in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 羅澤南薦諸巡撫胡林翼，檄領副後營，擢千總。

translations.literal: Luo Zinan recommended him to Governor Hu Linyi, who issued an order appointing him to lead the deputy rear battalion; he was promoted to company commander.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Zinan recommended him to Governor Hu Linyi, who ordered him to take command of the deputy rear battalion and promoted him to company commander.

sentences.zh: 咸豐六年，從騰鴻援江西，戰瑞州，騰鴻中砲殞，連捷率所部攻城，拔之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xianfeng he followed Tenghong to relieve Jiangxi and fought at Ruizhou. Tenghong was killed by cannon fire; Lianjie led his troops to storm the city and took it.
translations.idiomatic: In 1856 he marched with Tenghong to relieve Jiangxi and fought at Ruizhou. When Tenghong was killed by shellfire, Lianjie led his men in an assault and captured the city.

sentences.zh: 為曾國籓所重，薦改文職，以知縣留江西補用。

translations.literal: He was highly regarded by Zeng Guofan, who recommended him for transfer to civil office, to be appointed as magistrate and retained for assignment in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan thought highly of him and recommended that he be transferred to civil service as a magistrate, to be assigned in Jiangxi when a post opened.

sentences.zh: 從曾國荃克吉安，擢同知，赴安徽助剿，十年，大捷於小池驛，擢知府。

translations.literal: He followed Zeng Guoquan in capturing Ji'an, was promoted to sub-prefect, went to Anhui to assist in suppression, and in the tenth year won a great victory at Xiaochi Post Station and was promoted to prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Zeng Guoquan in the capture of Ji'an and was made sub-prefect. Sent to Anhui to help suppress the rebels, he won a major victory at Xiaochi Post Station in 1860 and was raised to prefect.

sentences.zh: 由集賢關攻安慶，破援賊。

translations.literal: Attacking Anqing from Jixian Pass, he defeated the relief rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Attacking Anqing from Jixian Pass, he routed the rebel relief force.

sentences.zh: 十一年，复破援賊於集賢關，克安慶，擢道員，賜號果勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he again defeated the relief rebels at Jixian Pass, captured Anqing, was promoted to circuit intendant, and was granted the title Guoyong Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1861 he again broke the relief army at Jixian Pass, took Anqing, was made circuit intendant, and received the title Guoyong Batulu.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，攻巢縣東關，賊立石牆於羅星山，連捷率死士夜渡河縱火燒賊營，進克西梁山、濡須口，渡江克太平府、金柱關、蕪湖，乘勝進軍江寧。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he attacked the eastern gate of Chaoxian. The rebels built stone walls on Luoxing Mountain; Lianjie led death-defying warriors by night across the river to set fire to the rebel camp, then advanced to capture West Liang Mountain and Rushukou, crossed the river to take Taiping Prefecture, Jinzhu Pass, and Wuhu, and pressed the advantage toward Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 he assaulted the eastern gate of Chaoxian. When the rebels threw up stone walls on Luoxing Mountain, Lianjie led picked men across the river by night, burned their camp, then took West Liang Mountain and Rushukou, crossed the Yangtze to seize Taiping Prefecture, Jinzhu Pass, and Wuhu, and drove on toward Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 連捷軍屯顏行，李秀成、李世賢糾大眾來攻，以炸砲破營壁，連捷築橫牆拒之，常乘賊懈夜出破賊壘。

translations.literal: Lianjie's army encamped at Yanxing. Li Xiucheng and Li Shixian mustered large forces to attack, using explosive cannon to breach the camp walls. Lianjie built transverse walls to block them and often took advantage of rebel laxity to sally out at night and destroy rebel fortifications.
translations.idiomatic: Lianjie's force encamped at Yanxing. Li Xiucheng and Li Shixian gathered a large army and blasted the camp walls with explosive cannon. Lianjie threw up cross-walls to hold them off and repeatedly stole out at night when the rebels slackened, wrecking their works.

sentences.zh: 及賊退，以按察使記名，加布政使銜。

translations.literal: When the rebels retreated, he was entered on the rolls as surveillance commissioner and given the rank of provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels withdrew, he was registered as surveillance commissioner and given the rank of provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 大營恃無為州通餉道，連捷率三千人往守，營城外石澗阜。

translations.literal: The main camp relied on Wuwei Prefecture as its supply route; Lianjie led three thousand men to defend it and encamped on the Shijian Mound outside the city walls.
translations.idiomatic: The main camp depended on the supply line through Wuwei Prefecture, so Lianjie took three thousand men to hold it and pitched camp on the Shijian Mound outside the walls.

sentences.zh: 二年，李秀成困以長圍，軍糧垂盡，彭玉麟勸突圍出，連捷誓死守。

translations.literal: In the second year Li Xiucheng tightened the siege with a long encirclement; military provisions were nearly exhausted. Peng Yulin urged breaking out, but Lianjie vowed to hold to the death.
translations.idiomatic: In 1863 Li Xiucheng drew a tight cordon around them and rations ran low. Peng Yulin urged a breakout, but Lianjie swore to die where he stood.

sentences.zh: 彭毓橘來援，合擊賊，走之，再复巢縣、含山、和州，賜黃馬褂。

translations.literal: Peng Yuju came to reinforce; they combined forces to attack the rebels and drove them off, then recaptured Chaoxian, Hanshan, and Hezhou; he was granted the yellow jacket.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Yuju arrived with reinforcements; together they struck the rebels and drove them away, then retook Chaoxian, Hanshan, and Hezhou. Lianjie was awarded the yellow jacket.

sentences.zh: 偕水師進攻九洑洲、下關。

translations.literal: Together with the fleet he advanced to attack Jiufuzhou and Xiaguan.
translations.idiomatic: With the fleet he pressed the attack on Jiufuzhou and Xiaguan.

sentences.zh: 三年，龍膊子山地道成，偕諸軍衝入城。

translations.literal: In the third year the tunnel at Longbozi Mountain was completed; he joined the various armies in storming into the city.
translations.idiomatic: In 1864 the mine at Longbozi Mountain was ready, and he charged into the city with the combined force.

sentences.zh: 江寧平，以布政使記名，加頭品頂戴，予騎都尉世職。

translations.literal: When Jiangning was pacified, he was entered on the rolls as provincial administration commissioner, given the first-rank cap button, and granted the hereditary office of Cavalry Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiangning fell, he was registered as provincial administration commissioner, given the first-rank cap button, and granted the hereditary rank of Cavalry Commandant.

sentences.zh: 湘軍凱撤，曾國籓留連捷軍三千人駐守舒城、桐城防捻匪。

translations.literal: When the Hunan Army withdrew in triumph, Zeng Guofan retained three thousand of Lianjie's troops to garrison Shucheng and Tongcheng against the Nian bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hunan Army marched home in victory, Zeng Guofan kept three thousand of Lianjie's men to garrison Shucheng and Tongcheng against the Nian.

sentences.zh: 會霆營叛卒擾江西，連捷督軍追剿，駐防吉安、贛州，會剿粵匪餘黨於廣東嘉應州，盡殲之。

translations.literal: When rebellious soldiers of the Lightning Battalion harassed Jiangxi, Lianjie supervised troops in pursuit and suppression, garrisoned Ji'an and Ganzhou, and jointly suppressed the remaining Guangdong rebels at Jiaying Prefecture in Guangdong, exterminating them completely.
translations.idiomatic: When mutineers from the Lightning Battalion raided Jiangxi, Lianjie led the pursuit, garrisoned Ji'an and Ganzhou, and joined in wiping out the last Guangdong rebels at Jiaying Prefecture in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 連捷以傷病歸，家居十載。

translations.literal: Lianjie returned home because of wounds and illness and lived at home for ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Wounds and illness forced Lianjie home, where he remained for ten years.

sentences.zh: 光緒中，曾國荃撫山西，奏起連捷練軍包頭，從國荃移屯山海關，又從至江南治江防。

translations.literal: During the Guangxu reign Zeng Guoquan governed Shanxi and memorialized to recall Lianjie to drill troops at Baotou; he followed Guoquan in moving encampment to Shanhaiguan, and again followed him to Jiangnan to manage river defenses.
translations.idiomatic: In the Guangxu era, after Zeng Guoquan became governor of Shanxi, he memorialized to bring Lianjie out of retirement to drill troops at Baotou. Lianjie then followed him to Shanhaiguan and later to Jiangnan to oversee river defenses.

sentences.zh: 十三年，卒，賜卹，贈內閣學士，建專祠，諡勇介。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he died; posthumous condolence honors were granted, he was posthumously invested as Grand Secretary of the Cabinet, given a special memorial shrine, and conferred the posthumous name Yongjie.
translations.idiomatic: In 1887 he died. The court granted funeral honors, posthumously invested him as Grand Secretary of the Cabinet, built him a special shrine, and gave him the posthumous name Valiant and Steadfast.

sentences.zh: =彭毓橘=彭毓橘，字杏南，湖南湘鄉人。

translations.literal: Peng Yuju. Peng Yuju, courtesy name Xingnan, was a native of Xiangxiang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Yuju. Peng Yuju, whose courtesy name was Xingnan, came from Xiangxiang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 從曾國荃援江西，積功敘縣丞。

translations.literal: He followed Zeng Guoquan to relieve Jiangxi, and through accumulated merit was promoted to assistant magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: He served under Zeng Guoquan in the Jiangxi relief campaign and, for accumulated merit, was made assistant magistrate.

sentences.zh: 及進安徽，小池驛、菱湖諸戰皆有功，又屢破援賊，累功擢知府。

translations.literal: When advancing into Anhui he distinguished himself in battles at Xiaochi Post Station, Linghu, and elsewhere, repeatedly defeated relief rebels, and through accumulated merit was promoted to prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In the advance into Anhui he fought well at Xiaochi Post Station, Linghu, and elsewhere, broke relief forces again and again, and rose by accumulated merit to prefect.

sentences.zh: 會諸軍下沿江諸要隘，渡江克太平府、金柱關、蕪湖，擢道員，賜號毅勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: When the allied armies descended the Yangtze strongholds, crossed the river, and captured Taiping Prefecture, Jinzhu Pass, and Wuhu, he was promoted to circuit intendant and granted the title Yiyong Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: As the allied armies pushed down the Yangtze, crossed the river, and took Taiping Prefecture, Jinzhu Pass, and Wuhu, he was made circuit intendant and given the title Yiyong Batulu.

sentences.zh: 大軍逼江寧，毓橘與諸將分路取丹陽鎮、秣陵關諸要隘，夷賊壘數十，進攻雨花台石城，賊死拒未下。

translations.literal: As the main army pressed Jiangning, Yuju and the other generals took separate routes to seize strongholds such as Danyang Town and Molin Pass, razed dozens of rebel fortifications, and advanced to attack the stone fortress at Yuhuatai; the rebels resisted to the death and it was not taken.
translations.idiomatic: When the main force closed on Jiangning, Yuju and the other commanders split up to take Danyang Town, Molin Pass, and other key points, leveling dozens of rebel works before assaulting the stone fort at Yuhuatai, which the defenders held to the death.

sentences.zh: 李秀成率眾來援，大營被圍。

translations.literal: Li Xiucheng led his forces to relieve the city, and the main camp was surrounded.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiucheng marched to the rescue with a large force, and the main camp was encircled.

sentences.zh: 毓橘方染疫，力疾禦戰，伺懈出擊，破賊壘。

translations.literal: Yuju had just contracted plague; straining against illness he fought in defense, waited for a lapse in vigilance to sally out and attack, and broke the rebel fortifications.
translations.idiomatic: Yuju had just fallen ill with plague, but he forced himself into the fight, waited for the enemy to slacken, charged out, and smashed their fortifications.

sentences.zh: 解圍後，毓橘與劉連捷援江北，合水師連复江浦、和州、含山、巢縣四城，江北大定。

translations.literal: After the siege was lifted, Yuju and Liu Lianjie went to reinforce the north bank of the Yangtze; together with the fleet they recaptured in succession the four cities of Jiangpu, Hezhou, Hanshan, and Chaoxian, and the north bank was stabilized.
translations.idiomatic: Once the siege was raised, Yuju and Liu Lianjie crossed to reinforce the north bank. With the fleet they retook Jiangpu, Hezhou, Hanshan, and Chaoxian in turn, and the north bank was secured.

sentences.zh: 削平江寧附近諸賊壘，毓橘功為多。

translations.literal: In pacifying the rebel fortifications near Jiangning, Yuju's contributions were the greatest.
translations.idiomatic: In clearing the rebel works around Jiangning, Yuju's service stood above the rest.

sentences.zh: 龍膊子地道火發，督軍衝入，手刃退者。

translations.literal: When the Longbozi tunnel was fired, he directed troops to charge in and personally killed those who tried to retreat.
translations.idiomatic: When the Longbozi mine blew, he drove his men through the breach and himself cut down several who wavered.

sentences.zh: 論功最，以布政使記名，予一等輕車都尉世職。

translations.literal: Judged foremost in merit, he was entered on the rolls as provincial administration commissioner and granted the hereditary first-class office of Commandant of Light Chariots.
translations.idiomatic: Ranked first in merit, he was registered as provincial administration commissioner and given the hereditary first-class rank of Commandant of Light Chariots.

sentences.zh: 尋授福建汀漳龍兵備道，未之任，曾國荃疏調毓橘統湘軍赴湖北，捻匪竄擾黃州、安陸，毓橘進剿，戰比有功。

translations.literal: Soon after he was appointed Military Circuit Intendant of Ting-Zhang-Long in Fujian, but before assuming the post Zeng Guoquan memorialized to transfer Yuju to command Hunan troops in Hubei; Nian bandits had raided Huangzhou and Anlu, and Yuju advanced to suppress them, distinguishing himself in battle after battle.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed military circuit intendant of Ting-Zhang-Long in Fujian, but before he could take up the post Zeng Guoquan had him transferred to lead Hunan troops in Hubei. Nian raiders were troubling Huangzhou and Anlu, and Yuju drove against them with repeated success.

sentences.zh: 同治六年，師次蘄水，毓橘率小隊數百，週覽地勢，至麒麟凹，賊大至，被圍，搏戰，死傷略盡。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tongzhi the army halted at Qishui; Yuju led a small detachment of several hundred to survey the terrain and reached Qilin'ao. Rebels arrived in great numbers; they were surrounded, fought fiercely, and casualties were nearly total.
translations.idiomatic: In 1867 the army camped at Qishui. Yuju took a few hundred men to reconnoiter and reached Qilin'ao, where a large rebel force fell on them, surrounded them, and nearly wiped them out in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 毓橘馬陷泥淖，被執，{罒馬}賊被害。

translations.literal: Yuju's horse became mired in mud; he was captured, {罒馬} and was killed by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: His horse sank in the mud; he was taken prisoner, {罒馬} and was put to death by the rebels.

sentences.zh: 事聞，詔視布政使陣亡例議卹，建專祠，贈內閣學士，諡忠壯，加騎都尉世職，並為三等男爵。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, an edict ordered posthumous honors according to the regulations for provincial administration commissioners killed in battle; a special memorial shrine was built, he was posthumously invested as Grand Secretary of the Cabinet, conferred the posthumous name Zhongzhuang, given the additional hereditary office of Cavalry Commandant, and made a third-class baron.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the throne, an edict granted him the honors due a provincial administration commissioner killed in action: a special shrine, posthumous investiture as Grand Secretary of the Cabinet, the posthumous name Loyal and Stalwart, an additional hereditary rank of Cavalry Commandant, and ennoblement as a third-class baron.

sentences.zh: =張詩日=張詩日，湖南湘鄉人。

translations.literal: Zhang Shiri. Zhang Shiri was a native of Xiangxiang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shiri. Zhang Shiri came from Xiangxiang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 咸豐五年，以外委隨羅澤南戰江西，克義寧。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xianfeng, as an external deputy he followed Luo Zinan to fight in Jiangxi and captured Yining.
translations.idiomatic: In 1855, serving as an external deputy, he followed Luo Zinan into Jiangxi and helped take Yining.

sentences.zh: 六年，改隸曾國荃軍，克安福，戰吉安。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to Zeng Guoquan's army, captured Anfu, and fought at Ji'an.
translations.idiomatic: In 1856 he was transferred to Zeng Guoquan's command, took Anfu, and fought at Ji'an.

sentences.zh: 八年，复萬安、吉水，超擢守備。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he recaptured Wan'an and Jishui and was promoted out of turn to garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: In 1858 he retook Wan'an and Jishui and was promoted ahead of schedule to garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 九年，以克吉安及景德鎮、浮梁，累擢游擊。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, for capturing Ji'an as well as Jingdezhen and Fuliang, he was promoted by accumulated merit to mobile corps commander.
translations.idiomatic: In 1859, for the capture of Ji'an, Jingdezhen, and Fuliang, he rose by accumulated merit to mobile corps commander.

sentences.zh: 十年，援小池驛，复太湖、潛山，晉參將。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he relieved Xiaochi Post Station, recaptured Taihu and Qianshan, and was advanced to brigade general.
translations.idiomatic: In 1860 he relieved Xiaochi Post Station, retook Taihu and Qianshan, and was promoted to brigade general.

sentences.zh: 從攻安慶，率三營破援賊於樅陽。

translations.literal: Participating in the attack on Anqing, he led three battalions to defeat relief rebels at Zongyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the assault on Anqing he led three battalions and broke the relief force at Zongyang.

sentences.zh: 十一年，克安慶，擢副將，加總兵銜，賜號幹勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Anqing was captured; he was promoted to deputy commander, given the brevet rank of brigade commander, and granted the title Ganyong Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1861, when Anqing fell, he was made deputy commander, given the brevet rank of brigade commander, and awarded the title Ganyong Batulu.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，從克沿江要隘。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he participated in capturing the Yangtze strongholds.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 he took part in reducing the fortified posts along the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 及抵江寧，力守大營，破援賊。

translations.literal: When they reached Jiangning, he vigorously defended the main camp and defeated relief rebels.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiangning he fought hard to hold the main camp and beat back the relief army.

sentences.zh: 累擢，以提督記名。

translations.literal: Through accumulated promotions he was entered on the rolls as provincial military commander.
translations.idiomatic: By repeated promotion he was registered as provincial military commander.

sentences.zh: 二年，屢破江寧城外賊壘，賜黃馬褂。

translations.literal: In the second year he repeatedly broke rebel fortifications outside Jiangning's walls and was granted the yellow jacket.
translations.idiomatic: In 1863 he smashed rebel works outside Jiangning again and again and received the yellow jacket.

sentences.zh: 三年，克天保、地保兩城。

translations.literal: In the third year he captured the two cities of Tianbao and Dibao.
translations.idiomatic: In 1864 he took the twin forts of Tianbao and Dibao.

sentences.zh: 方開掘龍膊子地道，李秀成夜自太平門突出來犯，又詐為官軍，別從朝陽門東隅出，偪營縱火，詩日偕諸將力戰卻之。

translations.literal: While the Longbozi tunnel was being dug, Li Xiucheng by night sallied out from Taiping Gate to attack; he also disguised his forces as government troops and sent another group out from the northeast corner of Chaoyang Gate to press the camp and set fires; Shiri joined the other generals in fighting fiercely and repulsed them.
translations.idiomatic: While the Longbozi tunnel was under excavation, Li Xiucheng burst out of Taiping Gate by night. He also sent men disguised as imperial troops from the northeast corner of Chaoyang Gate to press the camp and set fires. Shiri and the other commanders fought them off.

sentences.zh: 地道火發，城崩，詩日率士卒登龍廣山，奪太平門；

translations.literal: When the tunnel was fired and the wall collapsed, Shiri led soldiers up Longguang Mountain and seized Taiping Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When the mine blew and the wall gave way, Shiri led his men up Longguang Mountain and took Taiping Gate.

sentences.zh: 复循神策門轉戰至獅子山，奪儀鳳門。

translations.literal: He then fought along Shence Gate to Lion Mountain and seized Yifeng Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He then fought from Shence Gate to Lion Mountain and captured Yifeng Gate.

sentences.zh: 論功最，予一等輕車都尉世職。

translations.literal: Judged foremost in merit, he was granted the hereditary first-class office of Commandant of Light Chariots.
translations.idiomatic: Ranked first in merit, he received the hereditary first-class rank of Commandant of Light Chariots.

sentences.zh: 四年，授直隸宣化鎮總兵。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed brigade commander of the Xuanhua garrison in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In 1865 he was appointed brigade commander of the Xuanhua garrison in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 五年，從曾國籓剿捻，破張總愚、牛洛紅於西平，又敗之萬金寨，進攻雙廟賊巢。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he followed Zeng Guofan to suppress the Nian bandits, defeated Zhang Zongyu and Niu Luohong at Xiping, again defeated them at Wanjinzhai, and advanced to attack the rebel nest at Shuangmiao.
translations.idiomatic: In 1866 he followed Zeng Guofan against the Nian, routed Zhang Zongyu and Niu Luohong at Xiping, beat them again at Wanjinzhai, and pressed the attack on the rebel stronghold at Shuangmiao.

sentences.zh: 賊以馬隊襲官軍後，詩日分軍回擊，追敗之洪河，又敗之郾城、召陵。

translations.literal: The rebels sent cavalry to strike the government army's rear; Shiri divided his forces to counterattack, pursued and defeated them at Honghe, and again defeated them at Yancheng and Shaoling.
translations.idiomatic: When rebel horsemen struck the imperial force from the rear, Shiri split his command, turned on them, chased them down at Honghe, and defeated them again at Yancheng and Shaoling.

sentences.zh: 因傷發回籍，六年，卒。

translations.literal: Because his wounds flared up he returned to his native place; in the sixth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: Old wounds reopened and he went home; he died in 1867.

sentences.zh: 曾國籓疏陳詩日克復江寧，當西北一路，論功在李臣典、劉連捷、蕭孚泗之次，優恤，諡勤武。

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan memorialized that Shiri's role in recovering Jiangning, commanding the northwest route, ranked him in merit after Li Chendian, Liu Lianjie, and Xiao Fusi; generous condolence honors were granted, and he was posthumously named Qinwu.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan reported that in the recovery of Jiangning, where Shiri held the northwest sector, his merit stood after Li Chendian, Liu Lianjie, and Xiao Fusi. The court granted generous funeral honors and the posthumous name Diligent and Martial.

sentences.zh: =伍維壽=伍維壽，湖南長沙人。

translations.literal: Wu Weishou. Wu Weishou was a native of Changsha in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Weishou. Wu Weishou came from Changsha in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 從曾國荃援江西，攻安慶，克沿江要隘，擢副將。

translations.literal: He followed Zeng Guoquan to relieve Jiangxi, attacked Anqing, captured the Yangtze strongholds, and was promoted to deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: He served under Zeng Guoquan in the Jiangxi relief campaign, fought at Anqing, took the Yangtze strongholds, and was raised to deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 奪雨花台、聚寶門外石壘，累擢記名總兵，賜號毅勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: He seized the stone fortifications outside Yuhuatai and Jubao Gate, was promoted by accumulated merit to named brigade commander, and was granted the title Yiyong Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: He captured the stone works outside Yuhuatai and Jubao Gate, rose by accumulated merit to named brigade commander, and received the title Yiyong Batulu.

sentences.zh: 偕朱南桂破神策門，入城，率馬隊追逸賊至湖熟鎮，擒斬賊酋李萬材等，以提督記名，賜黃馬褂，予騎都尉世職。

translations.literal: Together with Zhu Nangui he broke through Shence Gate and entered the city; he led cavalry in pursuit of fleeing rebels to Hushu Town, captured and executed rebel chieftains including Li Wancai; he was entered on the rolls as provincial military commander, awarded the yellow jacket, and granted the hereditary office of Cavalry Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: With Zhu Nangui he broke through Shence Gate and entered the city, then led cavalry in pursuit to Hushu Town, where he captured and executed rebel leaders including Li Wancai. He was registered as provincial military commander, given the yellow jacket, and granted the hereditary rank of Cavalry Commandant.

sentences.zh: 六年，授陝西漢中鎮總兵，調甘肅寧夏鎮，光緒元年，卒。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed brigade commander of the Hanzhong garrison in Shaanxi, transferred to the Ningxia garrison in Gansu, and in the first year of Guangxu he died.
translations.idiomatic: In 1867 he was made brigade commander of the Hanzhong garrison in Shaanxi, then transferred to the Ningxia garrison in Gansu; he died in 1875.

sentences.zh: =朱南桂=朱南桂，湖南長沙人。

translations.literal: Zhu Nangui. Zhu Nangui was a native of Changsha in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Nangui. Zhu Nangui came from Changsha in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 羅澤南舊部，轉戰兩湖，積功至副將，賜號勗勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: A veteran of Luo Zinan's forces, he fought across the two Hu provinces, rose through accumulated merit to deputy commander, and was granted the title Xuyong Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: A veteran of Luo Zinan's command, he fought through Hunan and Hubei, rose by accumulated merit to deputy commander, and received the title Xuyong Batulu.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，解金柱關圍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he lifted the siege of Jinzhu Pass.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 he relieved the siege at Jinzhu Pass.

sentences.zh: 二年，克薛鎮、博望鎮，以總兵記名。

translations.literal: In the second year he captured Xue Town and Bowang Town and was entered on the rolls as brigade commander.
translations.idiomatic: In 1863 he took Xue Town and Bowang Town and was registered as brigade commander.

sentences.zh: 及克江寧，南桂先破神策門月城，梯而入，賜黃馬褂，予雲騎尉世職。

translations.literal: When Jiangning was captured, Nangui first broke through the barbican of Shence Gate and scaled the walls to enter; he was awarded the yellow jacket and granted the hereditary office of Cloud Cavalry Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: At the fall of Jiangning, Nangui was first through the barbican of Shence Gate and over the wall; he received the yellow jacket and the hereditary rank of Cloud Cavalry Commandant.

sentences.zh: 尋授河南歸德鎮總兵。

translations.literal: Soon after he was appointed brigade commander of the Guide garrison in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed brigade commander of the Guide garrison in Henan.

sentences.zh: 五年卒，賜卹，諡勤勇。

translations.literal: He died in the fifth year; posthumous condolence honors were granted, and he was posthumously named Qinyong.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1866. The court granted funeral honors and the posthumous name Diligent and Brave.

sentences.zh: =羅逢元=羅逢元，湖南湘潭人。

translations.literal: Luo Fengyuan. Luo Fengyuan was a native of Xiangtan in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Fengyuan. Luo Fengyuan came from Xiangtan in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 由武生入伍，從剿廣西。

translations.literal: Having entered the army as a military licentiate, he participated in suppressing Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the army as a military licentiate and took part in the suppression of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 曾國籓治水師，充營官，轉戰湖北、江西，累擢副將。

translations.literal: When Zeng Guofan organized the naval forces, he served as battalion officer, fought in Hubei and Jiangxi, and through accumulated merit was promoted to deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Zeng Guofan raised the river fleet, Fengyuan served as a battalion officer, fought in Hubei and Jiangxi, and rose by accumulated merit to deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 繼從曾國荃克安慶，以總兵記名，賜號展勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: He subsequently followed Zeng Guoquan in capturing Anqing, was entered on the rolls as brigade commander, and was granted the title Zhanyong Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: He later followed Zeng Guoquan in the capture of Anqing, was registered as brigade commander, and received the title Zhanyong Batulu.

sentences.zh: 進克沿江要隘，抵江寧，還守太平，屯金柱關。

translations.literal: He advanced to capture the Yangtze strongholds, reached Jiangning, returned to defend Taiping, and encamped at Jinzhu Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He pushed down the Yangtze, took its fortified posts, reached Jiangning, then fell back to hold Taiping and encamped at Jinzhu Pass.

sentences.zh: 賊酋陳坤書大舉來犯，逢元堅守，屢戰，以少擊眾，擒斬逾萬，以提督記名。

translations.literal: Rebel chieftain Chen Kunshu launched a major assault; Fengyuan held firm through repeated battles, defeating superior numbers with fewer troops, capturing and killing over ten thousand; he was entered on the rolls as provincial military commander.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel leader Chen Kunshu attacked in force, Fengyuan held on through battle after battle, beating larger forces with fewer men and killing more than ten thousand of the enemy. He was registered as provincial military commander.

sentences.zh: 及克江寧，由南門舊陷口梯登，賜黃馬褂，予雲騎尉世職。

translations.literal: When Jiangning was captured, he scaled the walls through the old breach at the South Gate; he was awarded the yellow jacket and granted the hereditary office of Cloud Cavalry Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: At the fall of Jiangning he went up through the old breach at the South Gate on scaling ladders; he received the yellow jacket and the hereditary rank of Cloud Cavalry Commandant.

sentences.zh: 以傷發假歸，光緒四年，卒，賜卹。

translations.literal: Because his wounds flared up he took leave to return home; in the fourth year of Guangxu he died, and posthumous condolence honors were granted.
translations.idiomatic: When old wounds reopened he went home on leave; he died in 1878, and the court granted funeral honors.

sentences.zh: =李祥和=李祥和，湖南湘鄉人。

translations.literal: Li Xianghe. Li Xianghe was a native of Xiangxiang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xianghe. Li Xianghe came from Xiangxiang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 初從羅澤南，積功至游擊。

translations.literal: He initially followed Luo Zinan and through accumulated merit rose to mobile corps commander.
translations.idiomatic: He first served under Luo Zinan and, by accumulated merit, rose to mobile corps commander.

sentences.zh: 嗣從曾國荃，克吉安，復安慶，累擢副將，賜號著勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: He subsequently followed Zeng Guoquan, captured Ji'an and recaptured Anqing, was promoted by accumulated merit to deputy commander, and was granted the title Zhuoyong Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: He later followed Zeng Guoquan, helped take Ji'an and Anqing, rose by accumulated merit to deputy commander, and received the title Zhuoyong Batulu.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，從大軍進江寧，力守大營，破援賊，以提督記名。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he followed the main army to advance on Jiangning, vigorously defended the main camp, defeated relief rebels, and was entered on the rolls as provincial military commander.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 he marched with the main force on Jiangning, held the main camp under heavy pressure, broke the relief army, and was registered as provincial military commander.

sentences.zh: 三年，攻克地保城，先登，築砲台俯擊城中，地道始成。

translations.literal: In the third year he captured Dibao City, was first to scale the walls, built batteries to fire down into the city, and the tunnel work was then completed.
translations.idiomatic: In 1864 he took Dibao City at the head of the assault, threw up batteries to fire into the town, and thereby cleared the way for the tunnel to be finished.

sentences.zh: 論功，賜黃馬褂，予雲騎尉世職。

translations.literal: For his merits he was awarded the yellow jacket and granted the hereditary office of Cloud Cavalry Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he received the yellow jacket and the hereditary rank of Cloud Cavalry Commandant.

sentences.zh: 四年，授安徽壽春鎮總兵，從劉松山赴陝西剿捻匪。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed brigade commander of the Shouchun garrison in Anhui and followed Liu Songshan to Shaanxi to suppress Nian bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In 1865 he was made brigade commander of the Shouchun garrison in Anhui and followed Liu Songshan to Shaanxi against the Nian.

sentences.zh: 六年，戰洛川大賢村，中砲陣亡，賜卹，諡武壯。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, fighting at Daxian Village in Luochuan, he was killed by cannon fire; posthumous condolence honors were granted, and he was posthumously named Wuzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1867, at Daxian Village in Luochuan, he was killed by shellfire. The court granted funeral honors and the posthumous name Martial and Stalwart.

sentences.zh: =蕭慶衍=蕭慶衍，湖南湘鄉人。

translations.literal: Xiao Qingyan. Xiao Qingyan was a native of Xiangxiang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Qingyan. Xiao Qingyan came from Xiangxiang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 應募入湘軍右營，轉戰江西、湖北，積功至副將。

translations.literal: He enlisted in the Right Battalion of the Hunan Army, fought in Jiangxi and Hubei, and through accumulated merit rose to deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the Hunan Army's Right Battalion, fought in Jiangxi and Hubei, and rose by accumulated merit to deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 克太湖、潛山，以總兵記名，賜號剛勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: He captured Taihu and Qianshan, was entered on the rolls as brigade commander, and was granted the title Gangyong Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: He took Taihu and Qianshan, was registered as brigade commander, and received the title Gangyong Batulu.

sentences.zh: 同治二年，援江浦，复含山、巢縣、和州，加頭品頂戴。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tongzhi he relieved Jiangpu, recaptured Hanshan, Chaoxian, and Hezhou, and was given the first-rank cap button.
translations.idiomatic: In 1863 he relieved Jiangpu and retook Hanshan, Chaoxian, and Hezhou, and received the first-rank cap button.

sentences.zh: 三年，渡江會攻江寧，克上方橋，進鍾山，築三壘太平門外。

translations.literal: In the third year he crossed the river to join the attack on Jiangning, captured Shangfang Bridge, advanced to Zhongshan, and built three fortifications outside Taiping Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In 1864 he crossed the Yangtze to join the siege of Jiangning, took Shangfang Bridge, advanced to Zhongshan, and threw up three forts outside Taiping Gate.

sentences.zh: 城破，於缺口衝入，奪朝陽、洪武二門，賜黃馬褂，予雲騎尉世職。

translations.literal: When the wall was breached, he charged in through the gap, seized Chaoyang and Hongwu Gates, was awarded the yellow jacket, and granted the hereditary office of Cloud Cavalry Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: When the wall came down he burst through the breach, took Chaoyang and Hongwu Gates, received the yellow jacket, and was granted the hereditary rank of Cloud Cavalry Commandant.

sentences.zh: =吳宗國=吳宗國，湖南長沙人。

translations.literal: Wu Zongguo. Wu Zongguo was a native of Changsha in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zongguo. Wu Zongguo came from Changsha in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 以勇目從剿湖北，累擢守備。

translations.literal: As a squad leader he participated in suppressing Hubei and through accumulated merit was promoted to garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: Starting as a squad leader in the Hubei campaign, he rose by accumulated merit to garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，從曾國荃沿江東下，迭克要隘，​​功多，累擢參將，賜號資勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he followed Zeng Guoquan down the Yangtze, captured strongholds in succession with many contributions, was promoted by accumulated merit to brigade general, and was granted the title Ziyong Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 he followed Zeng Guoquan down the Yangtze, reducing fortified posts one after another with conspicuous service, rose by accumulated merit to brigade general, and received the title Ziyong Batulu.

sentences.zh: 二年，破聚寶門外上方橋、江東橋各賊壘，會水師破九洑洲、印子山賊巢，擢副將。

translations.literal: In the second year he broke the rebel fortifications at Shangfang Bridge and Jiangdong Bridge outside Jubao Gate, joined the fleet in breaking the rebel nests at Jiufuzhou and Yinzi Mountain, and was promoted to deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: In 1863 he overran the rebel works at Shangfang Bridge and Jiangdong Bridge outside Jubao Gate, then with the fleet smashed the enemy positions at Jiufuzhou and Yinzi Mountain, and was made deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 從李臣典重開地道，城賊防益嚴，砲彈雨下。

translations.literal: He followed Li Chendian in reopening the tunnel; the defenders in the city tightened their defenses increasingly, and cannonballs fell like rain.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Li Chendian in reopening the tunnel, while the garrison tightened its defenses and shellfire poured down without pause.

sentences.zh: 宗國手藤牌，持長繩，冒砲彈，狙行而前，抵城下測丈而返，始興工開掘。

translations.literal: Zongguo led with rattan shields in hand, carried long ropes, braved cannonballs, crept forward, reached the foot of the wall to measure and returned, and only then was excavation begun.
translations.idiomatic: Zongguo went forward under rattan shields, rope in hand, through the shellfire, crawling ahead to measure at the foot of the wall before withdrawing; only then did the digging begin.

sentences.zh: 大功克成，以提督記名，予一品封典。

translations.literal: When the great achievement was accomplished, he was entered on the rolls as provincial military commander and granted first-rank enfeoffment privileges.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, he was registered as provincial military commander and given first-rank enfeoffment privileges.

sentences.zh: 五年，偕提督郭松林剿捻德安，戰羅家集，中伏，歿於陣，依提督例賜卹，予騎都尉世職。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, together with Provincial Military Commander Guo Songlin he suppressed the Nian bandits at De'an, fought at Luojiaji, fell into an ambush, and died in battle; condolence honors were granted according to the regulations for provincial military commanders, and he was given the hereditary office of Cavalry Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In 1866 he joined Provincial Military Commander Guo Songlin against the Nian at De'an, fought at Luojiaji, walked into an ambush, and was killed. The court granted funeral honors due a provincial commander and the hereditary rank of Cavalry Commandant.

sentences.zh: =【論】=論曰：洪秀全踞江寧十有餘年，曾國荃於蘇、浙未定之先，孤軍直搗，城大援眾，事勢綦難。

translations.literal: Commentary. The commentary says: Hong Xiuquan held Jiangning for more than ten years. Before Jiangsu and Zhejiang were settled, Zeng Guoquan with an isolated army drove straight in; the city was large and relief forces numerous—the situation was extremely difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary. The historians write: Hong Xiuquan held Nanjing for more than a decade. Before Jiangsu and Zhejiang were pacified, Zeng Guoquan struck inland with a lone army against a great city and massive relief forces—an undertaking of extraordinary difficulty.

sentences.zh: 及援賊既破，困獸之鬥，人人致死，歷兩年之久，竟蕆大功。

translations.literal: When the relief rebels had been defeated, the fight was that of cornered beasts—every man fought to the death. After two years the great achievement was at last completed.
translations.idiomatic: Once the relief armies were broken, the defenders fought like trapped animals, every man ready to die. Two years passed before the great victory was finally won.

sentences.zh: 固由指揮素定，而在事諸將，同心效力，奮不顧身，其勇毅之烈，紀太常而光紫閣，無愧色焉。

translations.literal: This was surely due to settled command, but the generals in the affair united in effort and reckless disregard for their lives; their fierce valor was recorded in the Temple of Eminent Worthies and glorified in the Purple Pavilion—they have no cause for shame.
translations.idiomatic: No doubt the command was steady, but the generals on the ground fought as one, heedless of their lives. Their courage was entered in the Temple of Eminent Worthies and honored in the Purple Pavilion—an achievement without shame.

sentences.zh: 掇其尤者著於篇。

translations.literal: The foremost among them are gathered and set down in this chapter.
translations.idiomatic: The most distinguished of them are recorded in this chapter.
